result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.dispersion()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate dispersion between two nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L8626-L8726){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.dispersion(u, v, normalized=True) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Dispersion measures the embeddedness of a link in the network. A link between two nodes (`u` and `v`) has high dispersion when their mutual neighbors (friends in common) are not well connected to each other. This can indicate structural diversity in the network. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [u]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Source node (node ID or label). [v]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Target node (node ID or label). [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), normalize by the number of common neighbors (embeddedness). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The dispersion score between `u` and `v`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - higher dispersion indicates the link spans different network regions - low dispersion means the link is embedded in a dense cluster - useful for identifying bridges between communities ## Examples {.doc-examples} Basic dispersion calculation: ::: {#e904d737 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create a simple social network graph = ec.Graph() for i in range(1, 6): graph.add_node() for s, t in [(1, 2), (1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 3), (2, 5), (3, 4), (3, 5), (4, 5)]: graph.add_edge(s, t) # Calculate dispersion between nodes 1 and 2 disp = graph.dispersion(1, 2) # Returns a dispersion value, e.g., "Dispersion: 0.50" f"Dispersion: {disp:.2f}" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 'Dispersion: 0.00' ``` ::: ::: Using node labels: ::: {#b73ce005 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_node(label="Alice") graph.add_node(label="Bob") graph.add_node(label="Charlie") graph.add_node(label="David") alice = graph.get_id_from_label("Alice") bob = graph.get_id_from_label("Bob") charlie = graph.get_id_from_label("Charlie") david = graph.get_id_from_label("David") graph.add_edge(alice, bob) graph.add_edge(alice, charlie) graph.add_edge(bob, charlie) graph.add_edge(bob, david) # Check dispersion disp = graph.dispersion(alice, bob, normalized=True) # Returns a dispersion value, e.g., "Dispersion: 0.50" f"Dispersion: {disp:.2f}" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 'Dispersion: 0.00' ``` ::: ::: Normalized vs unnormalized: ::: {#3f9ae087 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_cycle_graph(6) nodes = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) # Normalized divides by embeddedness norm = graph.dispersion(nodes[0], nodes[1], normalized=True) # Unnormalized gives raw count unnorm = graph.dispersion(nodes[0], nodes[1], normalized=False) # Returns e.g., "Normalized: 0.50, Unnormalized: 1" f"Normalized: {norm:.2f}, Unnormalized: {unnorm}" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 'Normalized: 0.00, Unnormalized: 0.0' ``` ::: :::
